issues.description: Method Stock.getStockIngredients(): the template implementation declares the method as returning a List<StockIngredient> (template: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java, signature at line 17: 'public List<StockIngredient> getStockIngredients()'), while the solution implementation declares the method as returning a StockIngredient[] array (solution: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java, signature at line 14: 'public StockIngredient[] getStockIngredients()'). This return-type mismatch is structural and will confuse students which API to implement; it can also cause compilation/type errors when students follow one artifact and compare to the other. The problem statement UML does not specify this accessor return type, so the intended API is ambiguous.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter signature consistent across template, solution, and the problem statement. Preferred concrete fixes: (A) Change the template method to 'public StockIngredient[] getStockIngredients()' and have it return the internal array (this.stockIngredients) so it matches the solution; update any code/tests expecting a List to use the array. Or (B) change the solution to 'public List<StockIngredient> getStockIngredients()' (e.g., return Arrays.asList(this.stockIngredients)) and adjust the solution's callers accordingly. Also update the problem_statement.md UML to explicitly state the intended return type for getStockIngredients so students know which API to implement.
